accepted.s: What does the acronym RISAT stand for?
o: Resource Imaging and Survey Analysis Technology
accepted.x: RISAT stands for Radar Imaging Satellite. It carries a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) for radar-based imaging.
accepted.tq: Use the exact expansion of the satellite acronym.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the imaging capability of RISAT satellites?
o: They can image day and night and through clouds.
They image only during clear daylight conditions.
They use optical cameras and cannot image through clouds.
They operate only when there is no atmospheric moisture.
accepted.x: RISAT carries Synthetic Aperture Radar, enabling imaging during both day and night and through cloud cover.
accepted.tq: Identify the functional advantage of radar over optical imaging.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: RISAT-2BR1 was launched by PSLV-C48 in December 2019. RISAT-2, RISAT-1 and RISAT-2B were associated with PSLV-C12, PSLV-C19 and PSLV-C46 respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure launcher-satellite pair.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RISAT series:
1. RISAT-2 used an X-band radar and was built with Israeli involvement.
2. RISAT-1 carried a C-band SAR operating at 5.35 GHz.
3. RISAT-2B was intended for X-band surveillance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. RISAT-2 used X-band radar, RISAT-1 used C-band SAR at 5.35 GHz, and RISAT-2B was an X-band surveillance satellite.
accepted.tq: Check each technical specification independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: RISAT-2 was associated with which of the following combinations of purpose and co-passenger?
o: Border surveillance, anti-terror operations and flood monitoring, with ANUSAT as co-passenger
accepted.x: RISAT-2 supported border surveillance, anti-terror activities and flood monitoring. ANUSAT was its co-passenger.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite with its operational role and co-passenger.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which RISAT satellite was India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite?
accepted.x: RISAT-1, launched in 2012, was India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite and carried a C-band SAR.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the indigenous milestone from the later RISAT missions.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about RISAT-2BR1 is correct?
o: It was launched in November 2020 by PSLV-C49.
It was launched in December 2019 by PSLV-C48 and had nine foreign commercial satellites as co-passengers.
It was launched in 2012 by PSLV-C19 as India's first indigenous radar satellite.
It was launched in May 2019 by PSLV-C46 and carried a C-band SAR.
accepted.x: RISAT-2BR1 was launched in December 2019 by PSLV-C48, the 50th flight of PSLV, along with nine foreign commercial satellites.
accepted.tq: Reject options by checking both the date and launcher together.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: RISAT-2BR1 provided services particularly relevant to which sectors?
o: Deep-space astronomy, navigation and television broadcasting
Manned spaceflight, meteorology and ocean mining
accepted.x: RISAT-2BR1 provided services for agriculture, forestry and disaster management.
accepted.tq: Link the satellite’s remote-sensing capability with its stated application sectors.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies EOS-01?
o: EOS-01 is RISAT-2, launched in 2009 by PSLV-C12.
EOS-01 is RISAT-2B, launched in May 2019 by PSLV-C46.
EOS-01 is the renamed RISAT-1B, launched in 2025 by PSLV-C61.
EOS-01 is the renamed RISAT-2BR2, launched in November 2020 by PSLV-C49.
accepted.x: EOS-01 was formerly designated RISAT-2BR2 and was launched in November 2020 by PSLV-C49. The EOS naming system was adopted for Earth-observation satellites.
accepted.tq: Separate renamed satellites by matching both the old designation and launch details.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about EOS-09:
1. It was formerly designated RISAT-1B.
2. It carried a C-band SAR and had a mass of 1,696 kg.
3. It was successfully placed in orbit by PSLV-C61.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: EOS-09 was formerly RISAT-1B, carried a C-band SAR and weighed 1,696 kg. The PSLV-C61 mission failed after a pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the false outcome statement in an otherwise correct technical description.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The failure of the EOS-09 mission was attributed to which of the following?
o: Failure of the satellite’s solar panels after separation
A collision with a defunct satellite
A pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor
A fuel leak in the first stage
accepted.x: EOS-09 was lost after a pressure drop occurred in the third-stage solid motor of PSLV-C61.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific technical cause rather than the general mission outcome.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2019, RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using data from which system?
accepted.x: RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using NETRA data.
accepted.tq: Match the space-safety operation with the system that supplied the tracking data.
accepted.sec: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which student satellite was built by Anna University, Chennai?
accepted.x: ANUSAT was built by Anna University, Chennai, and became the first satellite built by an Indian university.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-satellite association as the deciding clue.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was India's first pico-satellite?
accepted.x: StudSat, developed by a consortium of seven engineering colleges from Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, was India's first pico-satellite.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the satellite’s class milestone from institutional milestones.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Satellite)
A. Jugnu
B. SRMSAT
C. SATYABAMASAT
D. Kalamsat-V2

List-II (Institution)
1. Sathyabama University
2. IIT Kanpur
3. SRM University

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding student satellites is correct?
1. Jugnu was a nano-satellite developed by IIT Kanpur.
2. SRMSAT was built by SRM University, Chennai.
3. SATYABAMASAT generated greenhouse-gas data.
4. Kalamsat-V2 was launched by PSLV-C44.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. These satellites were associated respectively with IIT Kanpur, SRM University, greenhouse-gas observations and PSLV-C44.
accepted.tq: Verify each institution, function and launcher before choosing the full combination.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Kalamsat-V2 is notable for which of the following?
o: It was India's first satellite built by an Indian university.
It was India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite.
It was the first satellite to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform and was the lightest satellite of its kind mentioned here.
It was the first satellite dedicated to education.
accepted.x: Kalamsat-V2, built by Space Kidz India and launched on PSLV-C44 in January 2019, was the first to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform and was the lightest.
accepted.tq: Identify the unique first associated with the satellite rather than its builder.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding AzaadiSAT?
o: It was built by Anna University and became India's first university satellite.
It was built by IIT Kanpur and launched on PSLV-C18.
It was launched on PSLV-C44 and used the PS4 stage as an orbital platform.
It was developed by Space Kidz India with 750 girl students of government schools and failed to reach orbit after launch on SSLV-D1.
accepted.x: AzaadiSAT was developed by Space Kidz India with 750 girl students of government schools. It was launched on SSLV-D1 in August 2022 but failed to reach orbit.
accepted.tq: Combine the builder, participants, launcher and mission result.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s: WESAT was developed by which institution and served which principal purpose?
o: LBS Institute of Technology for Women; measurement of solar ultraviolet radiation
Sathyabama University; measurement of greenhouse gases
accepted.x: WESAT was built by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Thiruvananthapuram, and measured solar UV. It was the first Indian satellite fully built by women students.
accepted.tq: Match the academic institution with the satellite’s scientific payload purpose.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s: WESAT flew on which mission and platform?
o: PSLV-C44 with the PS4 orbital platform
accepted.x: WESAT flew on PSLV-C58 using the POEM-3 platform in January 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch vehicle mission from the satellite’s institution and payload.
accepted.sec: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which country was NOT among the foreign satellite contributors to the PSLV-C37 mission?
accepted.x: The foreign nanosatellites on PSLV-C37 came from the United States, Israel, Kazakhstan, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the UAE. Japan was not in the listed group.
accepted.tq: Use the country list and identify the omitted nation.
accepted.sec: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about PSLV-C37:
1. It placed 104 satellites in orbit in a single launch.
2. The mission included 101 foreign nanosatellites from six countries.
3. It carried the Cartosat-2 series and two ISRO nanosatellites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites on 15 February 2017, including Cartosat-2 series, two ISRO nanosatellites and 101 foreign nanosatellites.
accepted.tq: Check the total and the components of the record-setting launch.
accepted.sec: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the mass and orbit details of PSLV-C37’s record mission?
o: Total mass 1,696 kg and sun-synchronous orbit at 800 km
Total mass 714 kg and low Earth orbit at 200 km
Total mass 1,378 kg and sun-synchronous orbit at 506 km
Total mass 1,950.5 kg and geostationary orbit at 74°E
accepted.x: The PSLV-C37 mission had a total payload mass of 1,378 kg and placed the satellites in a 506 km sun-synchronous orbit. The Cartosat-2 series alone weighed 714 kg.
accepted.tq: Keep the total mission figures separate from the mass of an individual payload.
accepted.sec: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As of the stated July 2026 figure, NSIL had launched how many satellites, including how many international or customer satellites?
accepted.x: NSIL was stated to have launched 141 satellites, of which 138 were international or customer satellites, as of July 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total from the international/customer subset.
accepted.sec: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes PSLV-C62/EOS-N1?
o: It was the 50th PSLV flight and carried nine foreign satellites.
It was the first PSLV flight and carried 104 satellites successfully.
It was the 64th PSLV flight, the 105th launch from Sriharikota and the ninth dedicated NSIL commercial mission.
It was the 64th PSLV flight and successfully placed EOS-09 in orbit.
accepted.x: PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 was the 64th PSLV flight, the 105th launch from Sriharikota and the ninth dedicated NSIL commercial mission. It failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage.
accepted.tq: Match the mission with its multiple numerical identifiers and avoid confusing it with earlier PSLV records.
accepted.sec: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission anomaly?
o: The mission was launched from Kourou by Ariane-5.
The mission was delayed because of a pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor.
The mission failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage.
The mission achieved a record of 104 satellites in one launch.
accepted.x: PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage. The pressure-drop failure was associated with EOS-09 on PSLV-C61.
accepted.tq: Separate similar launch failures by identifying the stage and nature of the anomaly.
accepted.sec: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country  [APPSC]

accepted.s: GSAT-7A, also known as 'Angry Bird', is primarily associated with which service and capability?
o: Indian Air Force; network-centric warfare and drone operations
accepted.x: GSAT-7A serves the Indian Air Force and supports network-centric warfare and drone operations.
accepted.tq: Match the military satellite nickname with its service user and role.
accepted.sec: Military satellites → service user + nickname  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5.
2. GSAT-7 provides secure naval communication and maritime surveillance.
3. GSAT-7R, also designated CMS-03, is intended for the Indian Navy.
4. GSAT-7B is associated with the Indian Army.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7R/CMS-03 is its naval replacement, and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.
accepted.tq: Verify each service assignment and operational feature before selecting the full code.
accepted.sec: Military satellites → service user + nickname  [APPSC]

accepted.s: GSAT-7R, also designated CMS-03, was launched on which vehicle and date?
accepted.x: GSAT-7R, or CMS-03, was launched on LVM3-M5 on 2 November 2025 as a replacement for GSAT-7 in naval service.
accepted.tq: Match the replacement satellite with its precise launch vehicle and date.
accepted.sec: Military satellites → service user + nickname  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EMISAT is associated with which organisation and function?
accepted.x: EMISAT is associated with DRDO and performs electronic intelligence (ELINT). It was launched by PSLV-C45 in 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the defence user organisation from the armed-service satellite operators.
accepted.sec: Military satellites → service user + nickname  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding military and surveillance satellites?
1. RISAT-2 series provides radar surveillance of borders for the armed forces.
2. Cartosat satellites provide high-resolution imagery useful for border surveillance.
3. EMISAT is intended for electronic intelligence.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. RISAT-2 supports radar border surveillance, Cartosat provides high-resolution border imagery, and EMISAT supports electronic intelligence.
accepted.tq: Combine related surveillance functions without confusing radar, optical imagery and ELINT.
accepted.sec: Military satellites → service user + nickname  [APPSC]

accepted.s: TSAT-1A was built by which organisation or partnership and launched using which vehicle?
o: Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic; SpaceX Falcon 9
accepted.x: TSAT-1A was a sub-metre optical surveillance satellite built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic and launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in 2024.
accepted.tq: Match the private builder partnership with the correct foreign launcher.
accepted.sec: Private surveillance satellites → builder + launcher  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about private participation in Earth observation is correct?
o: It was approved by NSIL and included only foreign satellite builders.
It was led by Tata Advanced Systems with no other private partners.
The constellation was led exclusively by DRDO without private participation.
IN-SPACe approved a PPP constellation led by Pixxel with Dhruva Space, SatSure Analytics India and Piersight Space.
accepted.x: IN-SPACe approved a public-private partnership Earth-observation constellation led by Pixxel, with Dhruva Space, SatSure Analytics India and Piersight Space.
accepted.tq: Identify the approving authority and the complete private consortium.
accepted.sec: Private surveillance satellites → builder + launcher  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under SBS-3, what proportion of the satellites is to be built by private industry?
accepted.x: Under SBS-3, 31 of the 52 satellites are to be built by private industry.
accepted.tq: Retain the numerator-denominator relationship rather than only the approximate share.
accepted.sec: Private surveillance satellites → builder + launcher  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes EDUSAT?
o: It was a navigation satellite providing civilian positioning services.
It was India's first satellite dedicated to education and enabled two-way satellite communication with classrooms.
It was India's first radar imaging satellite for border surveillance.
It was a military communication satellite used exclusively by the Navy.
accepted.x: GSAT-3, popularly known as EDUSAT, was India's first satellite dedicated to education and provided two-way satellite communication to classrooms.
accepted.tq: Identify the satellite from its distinctive national first and principal purpose.
accepted.sec: EDUSAT - purpose, FIRST, launch, users  [other exams]

accepted.s: EDUSAT was launched on which date and launch vehicle?
accepted.x: EDUSAT was launched on 20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01 from Sriharikota.
accepted.tq: Match the educational satellite with its exact launch date and vehicle.
accepted.sec: EDUSAT - purpose, FIRST, launch, users  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups correctly represents the users of EDUSAT?
o: Only defence laboratories and military services
accepted.x: EDUSAT served schools, colleges and distance-education networks through virtual classrooms.
accepted.tq: Infer the user group from the satellite’s education-oriented communication role.
accepted.sec: EDUSAT - purpose, FIRST, launch, users  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about EDUSAT:
1. Its lift-off mass was 1,950.5 kg.
2. It was placed in geostationary orbit at 74°E.
3. It was launched from Sriharikota.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. EDUSAT had a lift-off mass of 1,950.5 kg, was placed at 74°E in geostationary orbit and launched from Sriharikota.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical, orbital and launch-location details separately.
accepted.sec: EDUSAT - purpose, FIRST, launch, users  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which satellite is used by Swayam Prabha to provide 40 free DTH educational channels?
accepted.x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free direct-to-home educational channels.
accepted.tq: Separate the present educational broadcasting satellite from the original EDUSAT mission.
accepted.sec: EDUSAT - purpose, FIRST, launch, users  [other exams]
